atrial-fibrillation.rhythm: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response (91 bpm, irregularly irregular)

avnrt.rhythm: AVNRT (typical slow–fast): 174 bpm, narrow QRS, retrograde P hidden at the end of the QRS

avrt.rhythm: Orthodromic AVRT: down the AV node, back up the left lateral accessory pathway (narrow QRS, no pre-excitation)

ventricular-tachycardia.rhythm: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia, 182 bpm, with AV dissociation

torsades-de-pointes.rhythm: Torsades de pointes: polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, 271 bpm, the QRS axis twisting around the baseline (amplitude waxing and waning)

mobitz-type-2.rhythm: Sinus rhythm with 2nd-degree AV block, Mobitz II

complete-heart-block.rhythm: 3rd-degree (complete) AV block with junctional escape rhythm

right-bundle-branch-block.rhythm: Normal sinus rhythm; right bundle branch block

findings: Acute inferior STEMI: ST elevation in II, III, aVF
Reciprocal ST depression in I, aVL, V2–V6
ST depression in V1–V3 suggests posterior extension
T-wave inversion in I, V5, V6
The occlusion is proximal to the AV-node artery at the crux: slower AV conduction, longer PR
Acute lateral STEMI: ST elevation in I, aVL, V5, V6
Reciprocal ST depression in III, aVR, aVF, V1–V4
ST depression in V1–V3 suggests posterior extension
Pathological Q/QS waves in V5
Acute anterior STEMI: ST elevation in V3, V4
Hyperacute T waves in V3, V4
Old inferior infarct: Q/QS waves in II, III, aVF, T inversion in aVF, ST at baseline
Deep, symmetric T-wave inversion in V2–V4, no Q waves, ST near baseline, R waves preserved: Wellens pattern type B
Left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage (Sokolow–Lyon 5.2 mV) with repolarization abnormality (strain)
Right ventricular hypertrophy: dominant R in V1 (R 1.61 mV) with T inversion in V1–V2 (RV strain)
Ventricular pre-excitation (WPW pattern): short PR (76 ms), delta wave, QRS 146 ms. Repolarization changes are secondary.
Diffuse ST elevation (I, II, aVF, V2, V3, V4) with ST depression in aVR and PR depression in II (-0.09 mV): acute pericarditis pattern
Coved ST elevation ≥ 2 mm with T inversion in V2: Brugada type 1 pattern
Tall, narrow, peaked T waves (V3 11 mm): hyperkalemia pattern
Flat T waves followed by U waves (best seen in V2–V3), slight ST sagging: hypokalemia pattern
Long QTc (492 ms) from a long, flat ST segment with a normal T wave: hypocalcemia pattern
Short QTc (338 ms): the T wave starts almost at the end of the QRS (short ST segment): hypercalcemia pattern
J (Osborn) waves at the end of the QRS, long QT and bradycardia: hypothermia pattern
Right atrial enlargement (P pulmonale): P 0.39 mV in II
Left atrial enlargement (P mitrale): P 153 ms wide, notched in II (humps 56 ms apart)
